key_insight: The paper shows that Evo 2’s frozen internal representations already contain biosecurity-relevant signals that can be extracted with very simple probes. In particular, minimal linear and attention-based probes can detect antimicrobial resistance in metagenomic data without fine-tuning the base model.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of screening metagenomic sequences for biosecurity risks using foundation models, specifically asking whether dangerous biological features are linearly accessible in pretrained genomic embeddings.
method: Freeze Evo 2 and extract layer-26 activations from genomic sequences.
Train lightweight linear and attention probes on top of these fixed representations.
Evaluate probe performance on held-out metagenomic test sets for detecting antimicrobial resistance and related biosecurity signals.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that pretrained sequence models may be useful for security screening with minimal additional modeling cost. It also highlights a practical path for auditing model representations for biosecurity applications without modifying the foundation model itself.

paper_title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes
paper_authors: Jeremy Guntoro, Alexander Dack, Dylan Danno, Michaela Jančovičová, Križan Jurinović
